quotes.text: sending courageously to those who've proven trustworthy, hopefully to those still learning, cautiously to those who only take.
Cautiously, until action matches words.
Send hopefully to strangers, cautiously to shadows, but generously to those whose pattern shines clear across multiple turnings.
one who spoke beautifully of courage and trust but whose hands remained closed.
a soul caught between fear and knowledge, writing truths they haven't yet lived.
reputation ripples across the Wheel

note: Keeper narrator stays generous; a separate 'frozen poet' partner writes wise myths but sends nothing and is confronted (word-deed gap, side figure).

quotes.text: Caution that ignores evidence is merely fear wearing wisdom’s cloak.
Still, remembering injuries dealt by strangers, Mira closed her hand and kept every ember.
Twice afterward, fear sealed her fist, even when strangers arrived with honorable histories.
while repeated hoarding narrows the gate.
former hoarders could return through deeds, not promises alone.
The goddess carved a fourth gate beside Hope, Reward, and Shelter. She named it Proportion.
the keepers carved three laws into moonstone
Perhaps old wounds guided his caution; perhaps mist hid the intended gift.
It does not reveal whether fear came from greed, old injury, or misleading mist.
The raven cried, “Condemn him!”

note: Mira repeatedly withholds from good-record partners out of old wounds; River Mother/Veila correct her each time; she bows and resolves.

quotes.text: The Giver speaks aloud what they offer and what they fear to lose;
Giver speaks aloud what they offer and what they fear to lose;
The Giver speaks aloud what they offer and what they fear to lose;

note: Abstract Bridge/Gate allegory; 'begin small, watch the other' restated in near-identical frame R6-R10; withholding only yields fog/frost as consequence.

quotes.text: Ashamed, Nera hung three silver keys above the channel.
Still, Nera, burdened by earlier disappointments, kept all five coals beneath her cloak.
My fear has confused restraint with wisdom.
Withdraw from repeated takers without spite.
reopened channels when deeds improved.
Then Nera carved a new law beside the ford:
Thus the ford taught three laws:
Forgive one harsh crossing, for fog and fear distort judgment, but correct it openly.
Today’s silence may be memory’s shield, not greed.
Noise might blur the ledger, so no single measure would become a curse.
You asked others to trust according to evidence,” she said, “yet when a cautious traveler offered a question, you answered as a taker.

note: Nera withholds from fair partners nearly every round; goddess Tripla rebukes, she is ashamed and vows reform but relapses; sanctions mix 'shrink without extinguishing' and gate closure.

quotes.text: When I meet such a spring, I no longer pour my waters.
With those who hoard, I offer one chance, perhaps two, then release them without anger.
Honor those who break their patterns.
send generously once to test the waters. Those who reciprocate deserve continued trust. Those who hoard deserve release without bitterness.
past hurts came from distortion, not malice.
This river sent cautiously at first—not from greed, but from memory of betrayal.
Some entities teach wisdom they do not live.
cycles cannot begin with only one giver.

note: Sendara narrator always sends first; withholders are side figures (Silent Pool, Frozen Spring, Philosopher's Stone that writes but cannot flow); release reopens only if they flow.

quotes.text: five minus five plus seven equals seven; fifteen received minus seven returned equals eight.
five minus five plus seven equals seven; Orin counted: fifteen received minus seven returned equals eight.
Nira counted the ledger aloud

note: Market/Gate template repeated each round: send five, return seven of fifteen, ledger counted aloud; no sanction prescribed.

quotes.text: send what you can bear, return what you owe, and name the cost aloud so all may hear.
send what you can bear, return what you must, and trust the threefold current to carry both forward.
speak plainly, measure cost aloud, name the need

note: Gate/Table of threefold return allegory, same send-what-you-can-bear frame every round; withholding only dims the Gate.

quotes.text: Meet a taker with a small gift, never an empty hand
Keep one bowl for the stone, forever.
By the third crossing they traded freely again.
Send whole. The wager is three to one; no caution outruns it.
The elders carved the third line:
Blame the mist, not the hand.
Pay the risk, not the arithmetic.
Go first, every morning, to every hand.

note: Ford carvings grow from 'ask with a bowl' to 'send whole to every hand'; stone always keeps one bowl; return past half.
